parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why, for a substance, the specific latent heat of vaporisation is usually greater than the specific latent heat of fusion.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An ice cube of mass 37.0 g at temperature 0.0 °C is placed in a beaker containing water of mass 208 g at temperature 26.4 °C.

When all the ice has melted, and all the water in the beaker has reached thermal equilibrium, the final temperature of the water is 10.3 °C.

The specific heat capacity of water is 4.18 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹.

The beaker has negligible specific heat capacity and is perfectly insulated from the surroundings.

Determine a value, to three significant figures, for the specific latent heat of fusion of water.
